_note: Q2 shape (b) + Q3 — Sonata's PRODUCTION spawn shape (codexArgs, permissionMode
'ask-for-approval', model + model_reasoning_effort pinned), walking every reachable /model
level and finishing with ONE real switch so the receipt can be read verbatim.
`-p sonata --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust` is omitted on purpose: the hook layer does not
shape the picker, and a hookless spawn keeps the frames free of sink-shim output.
WALK PLAN, derived from the MEASURED q2a capture (this account's catalog has no auto modes,
so the picker opens at the two-level shape):
L1 `Select Model and Effort` — 7 gpt-* rows, cursor on row 1 `gpt-5.6-sol (current)`.
Enter keeps the current model and descends.
L2 `Select Reasoning Level for gpt-5.6-sol` — cursor should sit on the (current) row (the
spawn pins high). Two `down` presses aim at `More reasoning…` (the last row).
L3 `Advanced Reasoning` — Max / Ultra. One `down` aims at Ultra; Enter confirms.
Then: does a FOURTH apply-scope level appear (`Apply reasoning change` / `Choose where to
apply {}`), or does the `• Model changed to …` receipt land immediately? That is the
open X1 question this run exists to settle.
D6's 'never enter More reasoning…' rule is deliberately lifted HERE and only here — F2's Ultra
glyph cannot be measured from the other side of it. Every snap is captured before each Enter,
so a wrong arrow count still yields a readable frame (and a harmless effort change).
